answer: Every active agent signs an unbroken execution thread of sequential, client-audited work epochs to climb the protocol's trust terrace. Because routing rewards scale with the square of terrace height, splitting one worker's compute across $k$ clones divides each clone's thread length by $k$ and reduces total operator payout to $1/k$. To match one honest agent's influence across $k$ sybils, an attacker must pay for $k$ independent, non-parallelizable streams of audited work epochs, as buying self-dealt reviews emits a cyclic settlement ripple that forfeits both parties' accrued epochs.
